text:
maria: noticing weird east-west failures starting ~02:10 UTC. GPU workload pods in namespace gpu-inference losing connectivity to infra-cache (redis) and to other gpu nodes. p50 fine, p95/p99 spike and some packet drops.

sam: saw alerts from netperf and some pod-to-pod TCP resets. can confirm egress from gpu-inference is being dropped intermittently.

liam: I just ran a quick traceroute between two gpu pods, looks like traffic is being denied before leaving the namespace boundary.

maria: can someone check NetworkPolicies? last config change was earlier this morning during the multi-namespace cleanup.

sam: grabbing current netpols from the cluster:
```
kubectl get networkpolicy -n gpu-inference deny-egress-all -o yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-all
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```

liam: ohhh that's the issue — that policy with an empty egress list blocks all outbound traffic from every pod in gpu-inference. it was meant for a different namespace. looks like a bad namespace label or wrong kubeconfig when applying.

katie: if that policy is global to the namespace, it also blocks RDMA setup packets for the gpudriver pods and MTU negotiation, which explains the intermittent RDMA failures and higher packet loss on long flows.

maria: rollout-bot shows the policy was applied by a script earlier in the morning (auth: infra-automation). deploy-bot: can you show who invoked the change?

deploy-bot: infra-automation applied networkpolicy/deny-egress-all to namespace gpu-inference at 2026-03-18T02:03:12Z (run-id: ci-7890).

sam: mitigation: deleting the policy restores connectivity. but we should be careful — the intent was to lock down a different namespace (gpu-ops).

liam: steps I ran: 1) kubectl delete netpol deny-egress-all -n gpu-inference 2) restart a couple of affected pods to re-establish RDMA sessions 3) verify MTU and RDMA link up with "ip link" and ibstat.

maria: after delete, p99 dropped back to expected. redis connections recovered. GPUs reported lower SLI errors.

katie: we need a postmortem and a guard to prevent cross-namespace netpol apply. suggestion: CI job should require an explicit --namespace flag and verify target namespace label. also add a dry-run and approval step when a NetworkPolicy affects more than X pods.

sam: +1. also recommend pre-flight check that detects policies that have podSelector: {} and egress: [] or ingress: [] (explicit deny-all) and fail unless flagged.

liam: can add a quick script to infra-automation to parse the yaml and abort if namespace != intended and deny-all pattern present. I can PR in the next hour.

maria: logging note for tracking cost and capacity impact: this incident caused ~2 hours of degraded throughput for the gpu pool, increasing retry traffic and transient overprovisioning in us-west-2b. estimate ~1.2k USD in extra cloud egress + preemptible GPU retries. include in the postmortem.

katie: filing incident ticket and adding owners. we'll also whitelist internal infra-cache CIDR for the gpu-inference namespace until the guard rails are in place.

sam: anything else to check? I also want to validate that there aren't lingering iptables rules from CNI that magnify deny-all effects when combined with host-level firewalls.

maria: good call — liam can you run a quick host-level iptables-save on affected nodes and paste if you see unexpected DROP rules?

liam: will do. grabbing output now and will attach to the incident.

maria: thanks everyone — reconnecting to redis looks green. keep an eye on RDMA link flaps for the next 24h.

katie: noted. creating follow-ups: 1) CI guard 2) policy review 3) incident write-up 4) cost reconciliation.

sam: marking this thread resolved when postmortem lands. :thumbsup:
